scientific_question: Within the same 194+ original Illinois study GPS calendar-day source frame, is the recorded NIGHT−DAY GPS displacement q temporally differentiated across native Canis latrans, Lynx rufus and Odocoileus virginianus when ALL THREE taxa are observed on the SAME dates? Does the q difference with a herbivore agree with or differ from the predator-predator ordering? Do not infer actual predation or behavior transitions.
selection: All three native taxa that were fixed for this original source before the new time outcome. Do not add or remove a taxon based on its q sign. Since Illinois q signs already known, all three-species comparisons are explicitly exploratory and can be unsupported.
source_first_integrity: Require original Movebank provider bitstream UUID/bytes/MD5, hourly selected fixes and native tagged animal counts (from October 25), and q, q~daylength full-source n/mean originally frozen by PR16 to 1e-12 BEFORE recomputing any three-native source coobserved-day q effect.
q: Original timestamp-only at most one fix per UTC-hour bin; >=3 accepted DAY and >=3 accepted NIGHT straight-line GPS displacement steps on same astronomical date, within animal-year >=10 eligible dates. Raw 0.5–2h actual interval, speed <=60km/h, same solar period at start/midpoint/end.
shared_dates: Iterative fixed-point intersection of source astronomy (year,solar date) among ALL three native species, retaining native original tagged-animal-year with >=10 shared original qualified dates and >=0.5 h daylength support at fixed 43°N reference. Eligibility only from date support, NEVER observed q values or species signs.
sample_units: Within each taxon equal available calendar-year q and slope contributions per original tagged animal. Between each taxon pair, separately resample original tagged individuals (2000 reps; n>=5 for each source native taxon), preserving same shared source calendar-day frame. For datewise q difference vs daylength resample year-month blocks (>=5 blocks and >=20 source days).
estimands: mean observed source tagged animal q and q~43N daylength for all three native taxa on common shared dates
3 original native species pair q differences with source tag bootstrap 95%
3 native source pair q~daylength slope differences and source calendar month-block q-difference slope, each with explicit support
limits: One source field study only, not three independent ecological populations or two geographic replications.
All three native q and daylength source effects already examined in Illinois after PR16; this is a posthoc shared-source support restriction, not a blind confirmation or a new species selection.
Same source original calendar date does not imply identical sampled GPS UTC hours, microhabitats, experienced temperature, sunlight, predator-prey encounters or physical movement trajectories.
GPS q is log1p NIGHT−DAY observed displacement speed, not true proportion of active time, predator success, prey avoidance, competition, or niche partition measured by occupancy.

Minimum five ORIGINAL tagged animals per taxon for descriptive source-bootstrap; any unsupported 3-native shared calendar must remain unavailable rather than drop the deer or substitute 2-native dates.

8 original study macroestimates and their SOURCE weighting remain unaltered. Earlier ERA5 source raw JSON twelve HOLDS and preregistered 48-source signed shortwave direction negative external replication unchanged.
Privacy: source native taxon/DOI and aggregate support only; no original animal IDs, exact times/dates, coordinates, grids or per-animal q/slope values.
